pages.quiz:
ENGLISH ACTIVITIES — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #9
====

GRADE: Grade 1
SUBJECT: ENGLISH ACTIVITIES
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Attentive listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Attentive listening.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Attentive listening.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Attentive listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

2. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. goed
   B. goes
   C. went
   D. going

3. When practising Pre-Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre-Writing.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre-Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Pre-Writing.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

4. When practising Phonics, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Phonics.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonics.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonics.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

5. When practising Word Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Word Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Word Reading.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Word Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

6. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. run

7. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only an action
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a joining word
   D. Only a describing word

8. When practising Connected text and fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Connected text and fluency.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Connected text and fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Connected text and fluency.

9. When practising Handwriting, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Handwriting.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Handwriting.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Handwriting.

10. When practising Pre Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pre Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Pre Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pre Reading.

11. When practising Language School, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Language School.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Language School.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Language School.

12. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. No full stops
   C. Only one word repeated
   D. One main idea with supporting sentences

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Phonics and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Word Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Connected text and fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Attentive listening.

2. C — went

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre-Writing.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonics.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Word Reading.

6. D — run

7. B — A person, place, thing, or idea

8. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Connected text and fluency.

9. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Handwriting.

10. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pre Reading.

11. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Language School.

12. D — One main idea with supporting sentences

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Phonics; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Word Reading; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Connected text and fluency; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
